items.title: Make one executable task model own blockers, Genius routing, startup pressure, and queue truth.
items.why: The canonical ops blocker-preflight hand-parses only a narrow subset, the richer entrypoint depends on parseHumanItems(), and that parser rejects the live board's unbolded checkbox form. Cross-repo, task-work, and startup code carry still more parsers, allowing the same task to be executable, invisible, or human-blocked depending on the caller.
items.recipe: Extend the shared task-board library into a bounded AST for checkbox and table rows with section, checked state, title, description, tags, age, status, and source line. Route local blocker-preflight, ops, task-work, cross-repo task loading, and startup pressure through it. Add fixtures copied from the live board and a reconciliation receipt proving parsed open counts against raw checkbox/table counts.
items.verificationPremise: Studio Oracle evidence-found (17 hits); direct live-board fixture proves current unbolded Human Action Required rows.

L1.recipe: Accept plain and bold checkbox forms in parseHumanItems and route ops blocker-preflight through it.

L2.recipe: Add the shared AST, migrate every local task consumer, and fixture all live forms.

L3.recipe: Add source-count reconciliation, reason-coded executable status, and a drift ratchet forbidding new private parsers.

items.title: Turn the declared PROJECT_STATUS writer into the actual atomic mutation boundary.
items.why: The shared writer enforces SIL invariants, but multiple scripts still read-modify-write PROJECT_STATUS.json directly. A passing invariant check can therefore be followed by a clobber or score drift, and the current helper itself writes non-atomically.
items.recipe: Upgrade writeProjectStatus/updateProjectStatus to write a same-directory temporary file and rename atomically, preserving invariant enforcement. Migrate every direct local writer, add merge/invariant/atomicity tests, and add a source ratchet that permits PROJECT_STATUS writes only through the shared library and its CLI.
items.verificationPremise: Oracle lexical verdict was no-evidence; direct inspection proves bypasses in check-last-session-summary, render-startup-brief, verify-plan-mode, closeout-autopilot, and run-tests.

L1.recipe: Migrate the known direct writers to updateProjectStatus.

L2.recipe: Add atomic replacement plus invariant and merge tests.

L3.recipe: Add a source boundary ratchet and a deterministic mutation receipt exercised by startup and closeout.

items.title: Close the local Playtest Pulse around answer, continuation, and RUN THE FIX.
items.why: The primary RUN THE FIX path never records the playtest continuation. The shared continuation recorder updates the active flight but does not persist the resulting Pulse, so answer-before-action ordering stores an incomplete aggregate. The most important replay-intent evidence is therefore systematically lossy.
items.recipe: Create one recorder operation that annotates continuation, records the continuation milestone, and upserts the resulting portable flight by flight ID. Call it from RUN THE FIX and every alternate continuation. Make answer and action ordering commutative, preserve opt-in/local-only boundaries, and test both orders plus duplicate clicks.
items.verificationPremise: Studio Oracle evidence-found (24 hits); DeathScreen lines 83-94 and 641-673 prove the split path.

L1.recipe: Record RUN THE FIX and persist the updated Pulse.

L2.recipe: Create one atomic helper with order-independent upsert and duplicate protection.

L3.recipe: Add a versioned completion receipt and exhaustive answer/action ordering fixtures.

items.title: Replace unreachable onboarding arithmetic with an evidence-backed First Three Flushes contract.
items.why: The card defines four stages, indexes with completed runs, and hides at three completed runs. Its final Run 3/Build stage can never be active, while the test checks only static copy. Run count also cannot distinguish an unverified control path from genuine progression.
items.recipe: Extract a pure onboarding-stage model keyed by total runs plus tutorial/input-calibration evidence. Define reachable Calibrate, Survive, Adapt, and Build stages, explicit completion reasons, and a bounded receipt. Render from the model and add 0/1/2/3+ run matrices with and without calibration evidence.
items.verificationPremise: Studio Oracle evidence-found; direct HomeV2 inspection proves four stages with a runs >= 3 hide gate.

L1.recipe: Fix the off-by-one hide/index logic and add transition tests.

L2.recipe: Extract the pure evidence-backed stage model and render it.

L3.recipe: Add reason-coded completion receipts and a full accessibility/test matrix.

items.title: Expose a truthful Prestige Pressure Gauge before changing the curve.
items.why: Level 25 resolves to 11,520 kills under the current formula, roughly 231-1,152 runs under the project's own 50/10-kill scenarios. The Upgrades surface states only the level gate. That may violate the no-manufactured-grind pact, but retuning without participant evidence would be equally dishonest.
items.recipe: Extend the existing progression runway model into a player-safe receipt: current level/XP, kills remaining, conservative run-range scenarios, assumption labels, and no completion-time promise. Render it beside Prestige, project it to the agent contract, and add formula/boundary/copy tests. Do not alter XP, costs, or Level 25 in this item.
items.verificationPremise: Studio Oracle evidence-found (9 hits); direct progression formula evaluation yields 11,520 kills.

L1.recipe: Show kills remaining and the explicit Level 25 formula.

L2.recipe: Add bounded run scenarios, assumption labels, and tests.

L3.recipe: Project the receipt to human and agent surfaces and bind future retuning to consented Pulse evidence.

items.title: Collapse three skill-cost ledgers into one self-validating execution-budget receipt.
items.why: The active library writes .cache/skill-costs.jsonl and session-floor reads it, while record-skill-cost writes skill-cost-ledger.jsonl and log-skill-cost writes ignis/output/agent-spend.json. The protocol checks presence of a producer whose records its consumer never reads.
items.recipe: Make record-skill-cost a thin CLI over lib/skill-cost-ledger, migrate any live callers, retire the unconsumed local producer, and make protocol drift behavior-probe the same ledger session-floor reads. Define the output as token/context execution efficiency under a flat-rate plan, never a dollar-spend alarm. Add schema, malformed-row, and reconciliation tests.
items.verificationPremise: Studio Oracle evidence-found (23 hits) including all three paths and the mismatched session-floor consumer.

L1.recipe: Point record-skill-cost at the canonical library/path.

L2.recipe: Migrate callers, behavior-probe the consumer path, and add reconciliation tests.

L3.recipe: Remove dead local producers and emit a source-derived execution-budget receipt with malformed-row accounting.
